scenes.headline: How to shrink a model's memory and reuse it
scenes.sub: Score the cache by rereading, then compress once.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Oskar. A long chat fills a cache of past tokens, and it gets huge. Let me show you how to shrink it and still reuse it.

scenes.text: Score the cache without looking at your question, by making the model reread the context, so one compressed cache answers any question.
scenes.label: The idea
scenes.say: The trick is to score the cache without looking at your question. Then one compressed cache can answer any question you ask later.

scenes.title: Score the cache by rereading it

steps.say: First, read the whole context once and store it as a key value cache.
Then ask the model to read that context again, straight from the cache.
Give each stored pair a score: the most attention it gets during that reread.
Keep the pairs that earned attention, and throw the rest away.
The scoring never saw your question, so this one cache serves any query.

left.title: Query-aware
left.say: The old way scores the cache against the current question, so it fits that one question and nothing else.

right.title: Query-agnostic
right.say: Score by rereading instead, and the same small cache holds up across every later question.

steps.label: full cache
steps.say: Here is the full cache, one cell per stored pair.

steps.label: keep 30%
steps.say: Keep about the top thirty percent, and the answers barely change.

scenes.label: less KV cache memory
scenes.say: That is three to four times less memory, and about twice the decode speed, with almost no loss.

scenes.text: Score the cache without your question, and you compress it once and reuse it for every answer.

recap: Compress once, reuse for any query
scenes.say: So: reread to score the cache, compress once and reuse, and get it three to four times smaller and about twice as fast.
